# dsh-workspace-rail
A workspace-first sidebar for DSH: pinned chats, projects as folders, live Recents and unread marker

A workspace-first sidebar rail for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) web GUI: Pinned
chats (folders include

d), Projects (isolated workspace folders with their own
instructions and files), a virtualized Recen

ts list ordered by the last
finished turn, graded transcript search, unread markers and a live brows

ed by the last
finished turn, graded transcript search, unread markers and a live browser tab
title.
Runs on DSH 0.2.x (tested on 0.2.1) and on DSH 0.1.5 with the same build.
## Install
Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-workspace-rail`, or from GitHub: `d
sh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-workspace-rail`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in the
profile bundles; restart `dsh

web` to load the host half. To work on a
checkout instead:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`lib/` is committed, so a plain install needs no build step.
### Options

Row options go in the `- id: workspace-rail` row of your profile
`cordis.patch.yml`, under `config:`

ow options go in the `- id: workspace-rail` row of your profile
`cordis.patch.yml`, under `config:`.
| Option | Default | Meaning |

| `enableRail` | `true` | Mount the rail in the web GUI. |
| `stripeEdge` | `right` | Edge of the co

lour stripe on chat, folder and project rows. |
| `recentsMaxRows` | `5000` | Cap on rows kept in Re

cents. |
| `projectsRoot` | `~/dsh-projects` | Where per-project folders are created. |
| `trustedHo
sts` | `[]` | Host names (besides loopback) the rail API accepts. Empty means the authorities DSH it
self trusts: every `--trusted-host` value of the `dsh web` command line, plus the comma-separated `D

SH_WORKSPACE_RAIL_TRUSTED_HOSTS` environment variable. |
| `enablePointerHealth` | `true` | Check th

at linked project files still exist. |
| `enableWindowsIndex` | `false` | DSH 0.1.5 only: transcript
-window bridge for search. |

If you serve DSH under a public host name behind a reverse proxy, you already
start it with `dsh web

--trusted-host app.example.com` (the core's own API
fence needs it), and the rail picks that up wit

.example.com` (the core's own API
fence needs it), and the rail picks that up with no extra setting.
## How it is built

Dual-face plugin (host and browser), the same harness contract as
`dsh-session-pin`:

- `src/index.ts`: host face. Serves the rail's own API and file store; on
DSH 0.1.5 it also register

s the `workspace-rail` settings namespace (see
"DSH versions").
- `src/client.ts`: browser face. Cat

alog sync (sessions and workspaces
snapshots), the rail panel (vanilla DOM, outside React's tree), v

irtualized
Recents.
- `src/scoring.ts`: pure 4-tier graded search scoring (title x40, doc
names and

tags x15, first 3 messages x8, last 3 messages x4, 14-day recency
decay, pinned x1.2 boost).
## Placement

The rail **is** the sidebar list: the browser face registers the
`sidebar.workspaces` seat at priori

ty -2, one below dsh-metafolder-plugin
(-1), which is one below the shipped browser (0). The header'

s
**Rail | Folders** switch unregisters the seat to reveal the folder view
underneath (nothing is hi

dden with CSS); a **Rail** button in
`sidebar.footer.action` brings it back. The choice is per brows

er
(`localStorage['dsh.workspace-rail.view']`). Hosts without a slot registry
fall back to a floatin

alStorage['dsh.workspace-rail.view']`). Hosts without a slot registry
fall back to a floating panel.

The rail hides the "Pinned sessions" footer button of dsh-session-pin, since
the rail's PINNED secti

on lists the same pins; pinning itself is untouched.
One CSS rule in `src/rail-style.ts` (`PIN_FOOTE

R`); delete it to bring the
button back.

Colours come from the host's `--dsw-alias-*` tokens, so the rail follows
light and dark mode and any

theme on top; a theme plugin can also set
`--tz-*` variables (accents, display font, radius, shadow

s). Subagent
transcripts are excluded from Recents; rows show a compact age and open the
chat on cli

Subagent
transcripts are excluded from Recents; rows show a compact age and open the
chat on click.

**Rename:** triple-click a chat title, or the row menu, Rename. Enter saves,
Esc cancels, clicking a

way saves. It goes through the host
(`ctx.sessions.binding(id).session.rename`), which also pins the

title
against automatic regeneration.
## Projects

Clicking a project opens its view inside the rail: **Chats** first (same rows
as Recents: open, rena

me, age; row menu, Remove from project), with
**+ New chat** (created and filed in the project, then

opened) and
**Add chats...** (a searchable picker). **Files** below: paste a path or URL
and press

Enter, or drop text paths; name and kind are inferred
(`src/files.ts`). Clicking a file opens it in

dsh-better-sidebar's editor when
that plugin is installed (optional `ctx.inject(['betterSidebar'])`)

; links
open in a new tab. Files the server cannot find are marked and can be removed
in one click.
Files are links only: nothing is copied.
Moves, removals and deletes apply immediately with an **Undo** toast.
### Projects are folders

Each project gets `~/dsh-projects/<name>-<id>/` (option `projectsRoot`).
**+ New chat** registers th

at folder as a DSH workspace (titled like the
[该节后续省略]
## Persistence and security

State lives in `~/.dsh/workspace-rail/state.json`, served by the rail's own
API (`/workspace-rail/ap

i`, `src/host/api.ts`), not by DSH settings: DSH gives
every non-loopback browser a memory-mode sett

ings scope, so writes there would
never reach the host. The browser loads the host copy first, merge
it adopts that state).

DSH does not authenticate plugin routes, so the API checks every request:
loopback peer (DSH behind

a reverse proxy on the same machine) and a trusted
Host; writes also need a matching Origin, the
`X-
Requested-With: dsh-workspace-rail` marker and the harness session cookie.
